name: limit_default_is_not_named_default
why: THE DEFAULT CONFIGURATION IS NOT CALLED «Default». It is called «Default<A macchina>», and the angle brackets are INSIDE the name that the APIs accept. `ShowConfiguration2("Default")` answers FALSE -- it raises nothing, says nothing -- and whoever did not look at the return value would go on drawing on the variant from before for the rest of the plan, with nothing in the finished file to notice it by: the geometry is consistent, the dimensions add up, it is just the wrong part.
_why_i_do_not_guess_it: And even if one wanted to, one could not. A part just born from the template of this company ALREADY HAS TWO real configurations that begin with «Default» -- «<A macchina>» and «<Saldato>», the pair of the weldments, and `GetConfigurationCount()` answers 2. Translating the short name would mean choosing one, and getting that choice wrong gives no error. The message says instead how the name is made, which is the only thing needed.

expect.why: AFTER THE REFUSAL WE ARE STILL WHERE WE WERE. A refusal that had already moved the document would be the worse of the two: an error to read and a variant changed all the same.

expect._why_true: AND THIS STEP COST A RED. `ShowConfiguration2` answers FALSE even when the configuration asked for is already the active one: that boolean does not tell «I did not do it» from «there was nothing to do». The refusal that came out of it said by itself that it was wrong -- «I asked to activate Left and now Left is active». Now the criterion is which configuration is active, and the boolean comes back here as information.
